info.title: Galinum API
info.description: Galinum's HTTP API. The SDK endpoints power the browser SDK. Management endpoints use a project secret; Galinum's hosted agent uses a scoped pk_agent_ credential and can mutate campaigns only through lease-fenced evaluation routes. Some Hosted agent and Usage operations are available only in managed Galinum Cloud; the self-host server returns 501 for those operations.

post.description: Upserts an end-user by your own user id and shallow-merges traits: sending one trait updates it without wiping the rest. Galinum enriches traits server-side with `$country`, `$region`, and `$city` resolved from the request IP.

userId.description: Your product's id for this user.

post.description: Records a behavioral event for a user — the substrate Galinum's agents analyze for campaign targeting. Tracking implicitly upserts the user, so it is safe to call for users not yet identified. When the event name matches the targetEvent of a goal linked to a campaign (via goalId), exposed deliveries resolve to converted automatically. Exposure is shownAt for web in-app and deliveredAt for email.

event.description: Event name. Use stable, snake_case names.

props.description: Optional event properties (max 4 KB serialized). The browser SDK adds `$current_url` and `$pathname` automatically.

get.description: Returns up to 100 in-app messages the user is currently eligible for. Galinum evaluates every window-eligible running campaign's targeting against the user's traits and event history, assigns an A/B variant (stable per user, weighted), and creates a delivery record in the queued state. Fetching does NOT count as an impression: report `shown` delivery feedback when the message actually renders (the React SDK does this automatically). A user gets each campaign at most once; resolved deliveries (clicked, dismissed, converted) don't come back. Pass `pages=1` to receive page-targeted campaigns and each message's `pages` patterns; the client is then responsible for matching them against the current path. If more than 100 campaigns need evaluation, the server returns 503 instead of partially serving them.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Your product's id for this user.

parameters.name: pages
parameters.description: Declares that this client matches page patterns itself. Without it, page-targeted campaigns are withheld (fail closed) and no message carries `pages`.

200.description: The user's eligible messages (may be empty).

503.description: More than 100 campaigns require evaluation, or bounded audience facts exceed local capacity.

post.description: Records what the user did with a delivered message. `shown` marks the impression when the message actually renders, without resolving the delivery; `clicked`, `dismissed`, and `converted` resolve it — the message stops being returned for that user — and feed Galinum's per-variant measurement. converted also resolves automatically when a tracked event matches the targetEvent of the goal linked to the campaign (via goalId).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The delivery id from the message payload.

type.description: shown = the message actually rendered (the impression; sent automatically by the React SDK — custom consumers must send it when they display the message, or it never counts as shown); clicked = engaged with the CTA; dismissed = closed the message; converted = completed the campaign's goal.

404.description: No delivery with this id exists for the authenticated project.

post.description: Uploads an image to attach to a campaign message. Send `multipart/form-data` with a single `file` field: PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF (animation is preserved), up to 4 MB and 4096×4096 pixels. File contents are verified — SVG and files whose bytes don't match their declared type are rejected. Returns an absolute HTTP(S) URL on the server's configured public origin; reference it as `media.url` when creating or editing a campaign. The image never changes the message's presentation — set `message.presentation` for that. Objects are immutable and retained; upload a new file to change an image.

file.description: The image file (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF).

url.description: Managed URL to reference as a message's `media.url`.

502.description: Storage error — the image could not be stored; try again.

503.description: Media uploads are not available right now.

post.description: Creates a web in-app or email campaign behind the same campaign model. Use either one `message` (a direct communication, one variant named "A") or an explicit weighted `variants` array. Pass `launch: true` to start delivery, or leave a draft. Email launch requires a verified project domain and a matching from address. Optional `deliverFrom`/`deliverUntil` schedule a future start and automatic expiry.

name.description: Internal campaign name shown in the dashboard.

channel.description: Delivery channel. Email content uses subject, previewText, Markdown body, and an optional CTA.

message.description: Single-variant shorthand: creates one variant named "A". Mutually exclusive with `variants`.

variants.description: Weighted variants for an A/B test (at most one control, at least one positive weight). Mutually exclusive with `message`.

reason.description: Concise note on why this audience was chosen or revised; stored on the immutable audience version.

oneOf.description: Inline audience: validated, canonicalized, and stored as an immutable audience version the campaign pins.

version.description: Pin a specific immutable version; omitted = the segment's current version, resolved atomically at write time.

oneOf.description: Pin a saved segment's audience version. Archived segments are refused (409). A `reason` is rejected here — the pinned version carries its own revision reason.

audience.description: Canonical audience union. `null` or `{ "kind": "all" }` targets everyone. `{ "kind": "expression", "expression": { … }, "reason": "…" }` authors an inline audience stored as an immutable audience version. `{ "kind": "segment", "segment": "id-or-key", "version": n? }` pins a saved segment version (omitted version = current, resolved atomically; archived segments are refused). Check expressions first with POST /api/v1/audiences/check. Mutually exclusive with the deprecated `targeting` field.

targeting.description: Deprecated shorthand for the same audience semantics (strict trait equality + events seen/not_seen, ANDed). Still accepted; normalized into an immutable audience version. Prefer `audience`.

pages.description: Web in-app only. Path patterns limiting where the message may render. Email campaigns reject this field.

goalId.description: Link the campaign to a goal in this project (400 if the goal doesn't exist here). Tracked events matching the linked goal's targetEvent automatically resolve the campaign's deliveries to converted once shown. Omit or pass null for no goal — direct communications never need one.

launch.description: Start the campaign instead of creating a draft. Email returns 409 until the project's sending domain is verified and its from address matches.

deliverFrom.description: Requested delivery-window start: epoch milliseconds or ISO-8601 with an explicit timezone offset (e.g. 2026-08-01T09:00:00Z). Nothing is delivered before this instant; combine with `launch: true` to schedule a future start. Must be earlier than `deliverUntil`.

deliverUntil.description: Requested delivery-window end: epoch milliseconds or ISO-8601 with an explicit timezone offset. Must be in the future; delivery stops automatically at exactly this instant.

schema.description: Exactly one of `message` or `variants` is required.

201.description: The created campaign, including its variant.

404.description: audience.kind segment referenced a segment or version that does not exist in this project.

409.description: An audience segment is archived, or an email launch is blocked because the project domain is unverified or its from address does not match.

503.description: Message media could not be verified because storage was temporarily unavailable. Retry the same request.

x-mcp.guidance: Classify the request as direct, outcome-measured, or optimized before you write anything, then use the smallest mode the user asked for. A direct communication is one message: do not add a goal, variants, a delivery window, an evaluation, or optimization unless the user asked for them. Treat ordinary announcements as direct even when the product has goals. Use a single message field for direct communication. Set a delivery window only from timing the user gave you, or after you resolve the missing dates with them. If the user said draft, propose, or prepare, stop at draft and never launch. Launch only when the user gave explicit launch, send, or announce authority. If launch authority is ambiguous, stop at draft and ask. Avoid overlapping audiences and delivery periods with other running or scheduled campaigns. Before you create, launch, or update a campaign, read recent agent runs and query running and scheduled campaigns as two separate paginated searches. Read every page through pageCount for both statuses before treating their deduplicated union as a complete point-in-time snapshot. Repeat both searches immediately before the write. Never claim protection against concurrent campaign changes. If a create call is uncertain, never retry it: read campaigns back and confirm what exists before you act again.

get.description: Returns the project's newest campaigns first in deterministic createdAt-then-id descending order, with delivery stats. Defaults to the first 100 campaigns, matching the previous unpaginated maximum.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only return campaigns with this effective status. `scheduled` and `expired` derive from the delivery window; `running` excludes campaigns whose window hasn't opened or has ended, and `paused` excludes those whose window has ended.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the campaign name.

evaluatedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds. The single instant used for filtering and for every `effectiveStatus` in this response.

x-mcp.guidance: Use status or q to narrow the campaign set. Read every page through pageCount before treating the result as complete. When querying multiple statuses, deduplicate campaigns by ID before reasoning about overlap.

get.description: Returns one campaign with its variants and per-variant delivery stats.

evaluatedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds. The instant used for this campaign's `effectiveStatus`.

404.description: No campaign with this id exists in the authenticated project.

patch.description: Edits any subset of name, targeting, message content, variants, and the delivery window. `message` only works on single-variant campaigns; `variants` entries with an `id` update that variant, entries without one create a new variant (variants are never deleted — retire one with `weight: 0`; a campaign keeps at most 10 variants, exactly one control, and at least one positive weight). Extending `deliverUntil` into the future resumes an expired campaign (a paused one additionally needs the `launch` status action).

reason.description: Concise note on why this audience was chosen or revised; stored on the immutable audience version.

oneOf.description: Inline audience: validated, canonicalized, and stored as an immutable audience version the campaign pins.

version.description: Pin a specific immutable version; omitted = the segment's current version, resolved atomically at write time.

oneOf.description: Pin a saved segment's audience version. Archived segments are refused (409). A `reason` is rejected here — the pinned version carries its own revision reason.

audience.description: Canonical audience union. `null` or `{ "kind": "all" }` targets everyone. `{ "kind": "expression", "expression": { … }, "reason": "…" }` authors an inline audience stored as an immutable audience version. `{ "kind": "segment", "segment": "id-or-key", "version": n? }` pins a saved segment version (omitted version = current, resolved atomically; archived segments are refused). Check expressions first with POST /api/v1/audiences/check. Mutually exclusive with the deprecated `targeting` field.

targeting.description: Deprecated shorthand for the same audience semantics (strict trait equality + events seen/not_seen, ANDed). Still accepted; normalized into an immutable audience version. Prefer `audience`.

pages.description: Web in-app only. Replace path patterns; null or [] clears them. Email campaigns reject this field.

goalId.description: Link the campaign to a goal in this project; null unlinks. Linking takes effect for target events tracked from then on — it never rewrites past deliveries.

message.description: Replace the content of a single-variant campaign (400 if the campaign has more than one variant). Mutually exclusive with `variants`.

variants.description: Variant patches: entries with an `id` update that variant, entries without one create a new variant (`message` required). Mutually exclusive with `message`.

id.description: Variant to update; omit to create a new variant.

deliverFrom.description: Replace the delivery-window start (epoch milliseconds or ISO-8601 with an explicit timezone offset); null clears it.

deliverUntil.description: Replace the delivery-window end (must stay after deliverFrom and, when set, be in the future); null clears it.

200.description: The updated campaign with fresh variants and stats.

404.description: Campaign not found — or audience.kind segment referenced a segment/version that does not exist in this project.

409.description: audience.kind segment referenced an archived segment.

503.description: Message media could not be verified because storage was temporarily unavailable. Retry the same request.

x-mcp.guidance: Change only what the user asked to change. Do not add a goal, variants, a delivery window, or optimization to a campaign that did not request them. Before you create, launch, or update a campaign, read recent agent runs and query running and scheduled campaigns as two separate paginated searches. Read every page through pageCount for both statuses before treating their deduplicated union as a complete point-in-time snapshot. Repeat both searches immediately before the write. Never claim protection against concurrent campaign changes. If an update is uncertain, read the campaign back before you retry.

post.summary: Launch, pause, or end a campaign
post.description: Transitions a campaign's status. `launch` starts a draft or paused campaign, `pause` suspends delivery, `end` stops it permanently — ended campaigns cannot be restarted. On an expired campaign (past its `deliverUntil`) only `end` is allowed; extend `deliverUntil` to resume delivery instead.

404.description: No campaign with this id exists in the authenticated project.

409.description: The transition is invalid, or email launch is blocked until the project domain is verified and the from address matches it.

x-mcp.guidance: This is the launch, pause, and end control. Launch only with explicit launch, send, or announce authority from the user. If that authority is ambiguous, leave the campaign in draft and ask. Before you create, launch, or update a campaign, read recent agent runs and query running and scheduled campaigns as two separate paginated searches. Read every page through pageCount for both statuses before treating their deduplicated union as a complete point-in-time snapshot. Repeat both searches immediately before the write. Never claim protection against concurrent campaign changes. If a launch call is uncertain, read the campaign status back before you act again.

get.description: Returns the campaign's per-user delivery feed (who received which variant, in what state), newest first.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only return deliveries in this state. `frequency_capped` is a permanent campaign-email skip caused by the project recipient's rolling 24-hour limit.

404.description: No campaign with this id exists in the authenticated project.

get.summary: Get exact event conversions by variant
get.description: Computes an exact aggregate at one instant without returning raw event or delivery rows. A delivery converts when its user has at least one matching event at or after channel exposure and at or before evaluatedAt.

evaluatedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds shared by every aggregate in this response.

404.description: Campaign not found.

get.description: Browses the project's identified end-users. Filters combine (AND). Use it to ground targeting in traits and activity that actually occur in your data.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the external user id or stored trait JSON.

parameters.name: traitKey
parameters.description: Trait to filter on; must be provided together with `traitValue`.

parameters.name: traitValue
parameters.description: Exact match on a scalar trait's text form. Only stored string, number, or boolean values match; must be provided together with `traitKey`.

parameters.name: activeSince
parameters.description: Only users last seen at or after this instant. Epoch milliseconds or an ISO-8601 date.

parameters.name: firstSeenSince
parameters.description: Only users first seen at or after this instant. Epoch milliseconds or an ISO-8601 date.

get.description: Returns total, active, and new end-user counts. Active uses `lastSeenAt` and new uses `firstSeenAt`, both measured from `startAt`.
Returns one end-user by Galinum id (`eu_…`) or by your own external user id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A Galinum end-user id or your external user id.

404.description: No user with this id exists in the authenticated project.

get.description: Browses one end-user's tracked events, newest first. The user is resolved inside the authenticated project first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A Galinum end-user id or your external user id.

404.description: No user with this id exists in the authenticated project.

get.description: Browses the campaign deliveries sent to one end-user, newest queued first. The user is resolved inside the authenticated project first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A Galinum end-user id or your external user id.

404.description: No user with this id exists in the authenticated project.

get.description: Browses the project's tracked events, newest first. Filters combine (AND).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the event name. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only events at or after this instant. Epoch milliseconds or an ISO-8601 date.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Only events at or before this instant. Epoch milliseconds or an ISO-8601 date.

post.description: Creates a business goal for the optimized-communication loop: a target event to move, binding guardrails, and an approval mode. Goals are optional — direct communications don't need one.

x-mcp.guidance: Create a goal only when the user asked to measure an outcome or to optimize toward one. Never invent a goal to accompany an ordinary announcement.

get.description: Returns the project's goals (up to 100, newest first).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only return goals with this status.

get.description: Returns one goal.

404.description: No goal with this id exists in the authenticated project.

patch.description: Edits any subset of the goal's fields. Explicit `null` clears `description`, `targetEvent`, or `guardrails`. Set `status: "archived"` to retire a goal.

404.description: No goal with this id exists in the authenticated project.

x-mcp.guidance: Change only the goal fields the user asked to change. Never introduce optimization the user did not request.

post.description: Records one agent decision — its input, output, and rationale — so the dashboard's agent feed shows what ran and why. Set `goalId` when the run serves a goal; omit it for direct communications.

kind.description: Step kind, e.g. observation, proposal, launch, evaluation, conclusion.

input.description: What the step looked at (max 16 KB serialized).

output.description: What the step produced (max 16 KB serialized).

goalId.description: Must be a goal in this project. Omit for direct communications.

campaignId.description: First-class campaign identity. Required for hosted evaluate, propose, mutate, and approval runs.

idempotencyKey.description: Unique per project. A replay returns the original run with 200.

200.description: The original logged run for an idempotent replay.

x-mcp.guidance: Log material decisions, proposals, and launches here. Reuse the same idempotency key when you retry, so one decision never produces two run records.

get.description: Browses the project's agent-run history, newest first — the agent's own memory of what it already did.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Set to `names` to add a top-level `references` map of goal and campaign names for the returned runs.

x-mcp.guidance: Read recent runs before you create, launch, or update a campaign, so you can see what another agent already did. Log your own material decisions with create_agent_run.

get.description: Returns the project's audience-authoring vocabulary in one bounded, context-efficient response: the supported expression versions, node kinds, operators per type, window units, and validation limits, plus what has actually been observed in this project — trait keys with per-type user counts, event names with user counts and recency, and top-level event property keys with observed types. Use this before authoring an expression instead of paginating raw users/events. Output is exact distinct vocabulary (not sampled); when a list is truncated by its bound the response says so via `traitsTruncated` / `eventsTruncated` / `propertiesTruncated` — absence from a truncated list is NOT evidence the field doesn't exist. Low-cardinality string traits also include bounded representative values.

expression.description: Supported versions, node kinds, operators grouped by value type, window units, and validation limits.

types.description: Observed JSON type → user count (e.g. `{ "string": 812 }`). Multiple keys reveal a type conflict in the data.

values.description: Bounded representative values, present only for low-cardinality short string traits.

traits.description: Observed trait keys, ordered by reach.

lastSeenAt.description: Epoch ms of the most recent occurrence.

properties.description: Observed top-level property keys with occurrence counts per JSON type.

events.description: Observed event names, ordered by reach.

post.description: Validates and evaluates an audience expression against the project's current users WITHOUT persisting or launching anything. Returns the normalized canonical expression, its stable hash, a derived readable summary, structured diagnostics (stable codes, JSON Pointer paths, bounded typo suggestions), a single `evaluatedAt` instant, the exact matching-user count, and a bounded sample of matching users. Use it to verify an audience behaves as intended before creating a campaign with it. Invalid expressions return 400 with error diagnostics.

sampleLimit.description: Matching-user samples to return (0 to skip samples).

segment.description: Saved segment to evaluate, by id (seg_…) or machine key. Provide exactly one of `expression` or `segment`.

version.description: Segment version to evaluate; omitted = current.

schema.description: Provide exactly one of `expression` (inline) or `segment` (+ optional `version`) — both run through the identical validator and evaluator.

expression.description: The normalized canonical expression (stable key order, event counts defaulted, membership lists sorted/deduped).

expressionHash.description: sha256 of the canonical serialization — equal hashes mean identical semantics.

summary.description: Deterministically derived readable summary. Display text, not a parseable format.
summary.example: trait plan is "free" and not (performed used_csv_export)

diagnostics.description: Warnings that don't block: unobserved traits/events (with typo suggestions), zero matches, and similar.

evaluatedAt.description: The single instant (epoch ms) every relative rule in this evaluation used.

matchedCount.description: Exact number of users currently matching.

totalUsers.description: Total identified users in the project.

traits.description: Only the traits the expression references.

events.description: Referenced event name → the user's occurrence count as evaluated, bounded by the published maxEvaluatedEventOccurrences limit (a value at the bound means ‘at least this many’).

samples.description: Bounded, context-efficient sample of matching users: lifecycle fields plus only the referenced traits and event aggregates.

segment.description: Present when the evaluated audience came from a saved segment.

400.description: Invalid request or invalid expression — the body includes `diagnostics` with stable codes and JSON Pointer paths.

404.description: No such segment or segment version in this project.

503.description: One user's bounded audience facts exceed local exact-evaluation capacity.

post.summary: Explain an audience for one user
post.description: Evaluates an audience expression for ONE project user and returns a condition-level evidence trace mirroring the expression tree — the debugging surface for "why did this user match?" and "why did this user not match?". Each trace node reports its JSON Pointer path, matched state, and the compact evidence behind the decision: observed value and type for field conditions, occurrence counts and window boundaries for event conditions, and per-child outcomes for groups. Uses the same evaluator as check and message eligibility, so the three always agree for the same user, expression, and evaluatedAt.

userId.description: The Galinum user id (eu_…) or your own external user id.

segment.description: Saved segment to evaluate, by id (seg_…) or machine key. Provide exactly one of `expression` or `segment`.

version.description: Segment version to evaluate; omitted = current.

schema.description: Provide exactly one of `expression` (inline) or `segment` (+ optional `version`) — both run through the identical validator and evaluator.

trace.description: Trace node mirroring the expression tree. Every node carries `path` (JSON Pointer into the expression), `kind`, and `matched`. Field nodes add `field`, `op`, `observed` (compact evidence — long strings truncated, objects reported by type), `observedType`, and a `note` for absence/type mismatches. Event nodes add `event`, `occurrences`, `required` count, and `windowCutoff`. Group nodes carry `children`; `not` carries `child`.

segment.description: Present when the evaluated audience came from a saved segment.

404.description: No such user, segment, or segment version in this project.

503.description: The user's bounded audience facts exceed local exact-evaluation capacity.

post.description: Creates a reusable named segment from a checked audience expression; version 1 is created atomically. Check the expression first with POST /api/v1/audiences/check. Pass `idempotencyKey` so retries return the original segment (200) instead of erroring; without one, a duplicate machine key is a 409.

key.description: Stable machine key, unique within the project: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores; must not start with "seg_" (reserved for opaque ids).

reason.description: Why this segment/version exists; stored on version 1.

agentRunId.description: Originating agent run in this project (400 if it belongs elsewhere).

idempotencyKey.description: Retry-safety token: the same project + key always returns the originally created segment.

200.description: Idempotent replay — the segment this idempotencyKey originally created.

409.description: A segment with this machine key already exists.

get.description: Compact list (up to 100, newest first): metadata, status, current version, and derived summary — the full expression is fetched intentionally via the detail or version reads.
Detail read: metadata plus the current version's exact canonical expression and hash.

404.description: No such segment in this project.

patch.description: Metadata edits (`name`, `description`) change no version. Replacing `expression` creates a NEW immutable version atomically and advances `currentVersion`; it requires `expectedVersion` (the version you last read) — a stale value returns 409 with the segment's `currentVersion` so you can re-read, re-check, and retry deliberately. Campaigns already pinning older versions are never changed. Archived segments accept metadata edits but refuse revision.

reason.description: Why this revision; stored on the new version.

404.description: No such segment in this project.

409.description: Stale expectedVersion (body carries `currentVersion`) or the segment is archived.

post.description: Removes the segment from new selection: campaigns can no longer reference it, and its rules can no longer be revised. Its version history stays readable and campaigns already pinning its versions keep delivering unchanged. There is no delete and no unarchive.

404.description: No such segment in this project.

get.description: The segment's immutable version history, newest first: hash, summary, reason, and provenance per version. Read one version for its exact expression.

404.description: No such segment in this project.

get.description: One immutable version with its exact canonical expression — valid forever, including for archived segments.

404.description: No such segment or version in this project.

get.description: Returns project-level pause, approval, daily-budget, concurrency, and AI-credit controls. Managers edit the human-configurable controls in the dashboard.

ai.description: Current-period AI-credit usage and the coarse pre-sweep limit.

monthlyLimit.description: The organization's monthly AI-credit allowance, set by an owner or admin. Defaults to 2500. Zero pauses hosted-agent sweeps.

post.description: Records one immutable usage row for a hosted-agent execution, and the billing report that tracks it. Galinum prices the reported per-call token usage. Repeating an executionId returns the original row unchanged and creates no second billing report. Only Galinum's hosted-agent key may call this endpoint; a project secret key returns 403, because agents you run yourself are not billed for AI credits. The JSON request body must be between 1 and 8,192 bytes, inclusive.

requestBody.description: Send Content-Type: application/json with a Content-Length from 1 through 8,192 bytes. Larger requests return 413.

sessionId.description: Optional session metadata. Stored only when this value is a string; other JSON values are treated as omitted.

model.description: Optional model metadata. Stored only when this value is a string; other JSON values are treated as omitted.

calls.description: Per-call usage objects. The server accepts at most 200 entries, but the 8,192-byte request limit is authoritative and may allow fewer depending on the included fields.

items.description: All counters are optional and default to zero when omitted or null. cachedInputTokens + cacheWriteTokens must not exceed inputTokens, and reasoningTokens must not exceed outputTokens; violations return 400.

200.description: The stored usage result. replayed is true when executionId already existed.

400.description: Wrong content type, malformed JSON, a non-object body, or invalid usage. Invalid usage includes an invalid executionId; calls that are empty, contain more than 200 entries, or contain non-object entries; invalid counter values; cachedInputTokens + cacheWriteTokens greater than inputTokens; or reasoningTokens greater than outputTokens.

403.description: A valid project secret key was used. Only Galinum's hosted-agent key may report AI usage.

200.description: Due campaigns plus project loop and budget state.

decidedContinuation.description: True when this due item resumes a human decision without spending another daily run.

404.description: Campaign not found.

409.description: The evaluation schedule is currently owned by a live lease or an unconsumed proposal. The error distinguishes a pending human decision from a decided proposal the agent has not acted on yet.

200.description: An exclusive bounded lease. decidedContinuation is true when resuming a human decision without spending another daily run.

404.description: Campaign not found.

post.summary: Release, reschedule, or conclude an evaluation

nextEvaluationAt.description: Null concludes evaluation. A non-null reschedule must be at least 60 seconds in the future and inside the campaign delivery window; a rejected value leaves the lease held for correction.

400.description: The reschedule instant is invalid, less than 60 seconds ahead, or outside the campaign delivery window; the lease remains held.

404.description: Campaign not found.

409.description: The lease is stale, expired, or not held; an approved proposal has not been applied; or null conclusion was attempted while the campaign remains eligible under an active goal. Approval and eligibility conflicts preserve a valid lease so the caller can correct them. Rejected proposals do not block completion.

status.description: The resulting lifecycle status for a status mutation; null for an update mutation.

403.description: Human approval is required or the exact proposal is not approved.

payloadHash.description: SHA-256 hash of the exact campaign, evaluation instant, and mutation to propose.
The exact payload a human rejected; never propose or apply it again.

404.description: Campaign or proposal not found.

409.description: The lease, evaluation, campaign, or approval no longer matches.

200.description: The existing exact proposal and current lease state.

201.description: A new pending proposal; the lease is released.

404.description: Campaign not found.

409.description: A new or different payload attempt failed because the loop is paused, the campaign or goal is no longer eligible, or the live lease or evaluation does not match. Exact existing proposals replay read-only before these guards while the queue evaluation and payload hash still match, returning truthful awaitingDecision and leaseHeld flags.

get.summary: Get current usage and serving state
get.description: Reports the organization's usage for the current billing period and whether each channel is serving. Check `serving` before diagnosing web in-app delivery and `emailServing` before launching or diagnosing campaign email. Billing and spend-cap changes are human actions in the dashboard.

200.description: Current-period usage for the owning organization.

get.description: Returns the project's headline counts at one evaluated instant. `activeCampaigns` counts stored `running` campaigns, so scheduled and expired rows are included.
Returns a merged feed of queued deliveries and newly seen users, newest first. Ties break by kind then id, and the cursor encodes that exact tuple so pages never repeat an item.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to read the next page. Null when the feed is exhausted.

get.description: Returns dense UTC day buckets for impressions, clicks, conversions, and events over the selected range, plus the range's top event names.

publishableKey.description: Your project's publishable key (`pk_pub_…`). Safe to expose in the browser — it identifies the project and is rate-limited, not secret.

secretKey.description: Your project's secret key (`pk_…`, without the `pub` segment). Server-side only — never ship it to a browser. Get it from Settings → Projects in the dashboard.

hostedAgentKey.description: Galinum's scoped hosted-agent key (`pk_agent_…`). It can read required project state and call hosted evaluation routes, but ordinary campaign, status, goal, segment, and media writes return 403.

Traits.description: User traits (max 4 KB serialized), shallow-merged into the existing profile. `$`-prefixed keys are reserved for auto-collected context (`$browser`, `$os`, `$timezone`, `$country`, …).

deliveryId.description: Use this id to report feedback.

pages.description: Path patterns this message may render on, or null for every page. Present only when the request declared `pages=1`.

content.description: The variant's JSON payload. The default shape is `{ title?, body?, cta?, media?, presentation }`, but campaigns may carry any JSON your renderer understands. Default-shape content always ships `presentation`; campaigns authored before it existed resolve to `modal` with media and `toast` without.

presentation.description: How the built-in renderer presents this message.

WebInAppMessageInput.description: The in-app message content. Needs at least a title or a body, and always states its `presentation`. An optional `media` image is content, not presentation: a toast shows it as a compact thumbnail, a modal as the immersive visual.

presentation.description: How the built-in renderer presents the message; media is independent content. `toast` is the compact bottom-right card, `modal` the centered announcement over a full-screen backdrop.

body.example: Export any table to CSV from the toolbar.

url.description: Must be https://, http://, mailto:, or a path like /billing.

EmailMessageInput.description: Email campaign content. The body is Markdown and Galinum adds the project compliance footer.

previewText.example: Download any table in one click

body.example: # CSV export is here\n\nDownload any table from the toolbar.

MessageInput.description: Channel-specific campaign content. Use the web in-app shape for channel web_inapp and the email shape for channel email.

StoredWebInAppMessageContent.description: The variant's stored message content. Same shape as the write schema, except `presentation` is absent on campaigns authored before it existed — reads return stored content verbatim. Delivery resolves one for those (media → `modal`, no media → `toast`).

presentation.description: How the built-in renderer presents the message; media is independent content. `toast` is the compact bottom-right card, `modal` the centered announcement over a full-screen backdrop.

body.example: Export any table to CSV from the toolbar.

url.description: Must be https://, http://, mailto:, or a path like /billing.

MessageMedia.description: Optional image for a message (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or animated GIF). Media is content, not presentation: a toast shows it as a compact thumbnail and a modal shows it as the immersive visual. Exactly one of `alt` or `decorative: true` is required.

url.description: A managed campaign media URL returned by POST /api/v1/campaign-media for this project. External, data:, and other projects' URLs are rejected.

alt.description: What the image shows, for assistive technology. Required unless `decorative` is true.
alt.example: Screenshot of the new analytics dashboard

decorative.description: Mark the image as purely decorative instead of providing alt text. Mutually exclusive with `alt`.

Targeting.description: Audience rules. All conditions must match. An empty object (or null) matches everyone.

traits.description: Trait values the user must match by strict equality.

seen.description: Events the user must have fired at least once.

not_seen.description: Events the user must NOT have fired.

frequencyCapped.description: Campaign-email recipients skipped by the project-wide rolling 24-hour frequency limit.

effectiveStatus.description: Lifecycle status refined by the delivery window, always current: `scheduled` = running before `deliverFrom`, `expired` = running/paused at or after `deliverUntil` (expiry outranks paused).

goalId.description: The goal this campaign serves, or null. When set, tracked events matching the goal's targetEvent automatically resolve exposed deliveries to converted. Exposure is shownAt for web in-app and deliveredAt for email.

createdBy.description: Who created the campaign: a dashboard user (`human`), this API (`api`), or the Galinum agent (`agent`).

deliverFrom.description: Requested delivery-window start, epoch milliseconds (null = starts when launched).

deliverUntil.description: Requested delivery-window end, epoch milliseconds (null = delivers until ended).

targeting.description: Deprecated legacy targeting shape, present only for campaigns still stored with it (null otherwise). Read `audience` instead.

pages.description: Web in-app path patterns, or null. Email campaigns always return null.

error.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

id.description: Galinum's id for this end user.

externalUserId.description: Your product's id for this user, as sent to identify/track.

traits.description: The user's current traits. `$`-prefixed keys are auto-collected context.

description.example: Get signups to create their first board within 7 days

targetEvent.description: The tracked event name this goal moves.

guardrails.description: Free-form JSON object of binding instructions for the agent.

approvalMode.description: `require_human` = the agent proposes and waits; `auto` = it may launch on its own.

kind.description: Free-form step kind. The galinum skill uses: observation, proposal, launch, schedule, evaluation, iteration, conclusion, rejected.

goalId.description: The goal this run serves; null for direct communications.

campaignId.description: The campaign this run serves; first-class for hosted campaign decisions.

rationale.example: 412 free-plan users active this week haven't created a board.

state.description: The latest resolution. The *At timestamps accumulate independently — a delivery can have both clickedAt and convertedAt. `frequency_capped` is terminal, has no sentAt, and does not accrue MAU.

sentAt.description: Email provider accepted the send, in epoch milliseconds.

deliveredAt.description: Email reached the recipient mail server, in epoch milliseconds.

openedAt.description: Email open event, in epoch milliseconds.

bouncedAt.description: Permanent email bounce, in epoch milliseconds.

unsubscribedAt.description: Project-wide email opt-out, in epoch milliseconds.

name.description: Defaults to A, B, C… by position.

weight.description: Relative assignment weight. 0 retires the variant (it is never assigned).

isControl.description: At most one control per campaign; defaults to the first variant.

key.description: Literal top-level event property key. Only valid inside an event node's where conditions.

AudienceWindow.description: Relative time window measured back from the evaluation instant (evaluatedAt).

oneOf.description: At least one child must match.

value.description: Required for every operator except exists/not_exists (which reject it). Typed per operator: eq/neq take a string/number/boolean; in/not_in a non-empty array (≤ 50) of all strings or all numbers; contains/starts_with/ends_with a string; gt/gte/lt/lte a number; before/after an ISO-8601 date-time with explicit offset; within_last/not_within_last an AudienceWindow.

oneOf.description: Compares a user trait or lifecycle field. Comparisons are strict — no type coercion; a value comparison on an absent or type-incompatible field does not match (use exists/not_exists for absence). Lifecycle fields accept only datetime and existence operators.

count.description: Occurrence-count comparison; defaults to at-least-once ({ op: gte, value: 1 }).

where.description: field nodes on event_property references, ANDed per occurrence.

oneOf.description: Evaluates occurrences of one event, optionally within a relative window and filtered by event-property conditions.

AudienceNode.description: One audience expression node, discriminated by `kind`. Overall limits: nesting depth ≤ 8, total nodes ≤ 64. Unknown kinds, unknown operators, unknown keys, and empty groups are rejected with structured diagnostics.

AudienceExpression.description: Versioned, strictly validated audience rule. Example: `{ "version": 1, "root": { "kind": "all", "children": [ { "kind": "field", "field": { "kind": "trait", "key": "plan" }, "op": "eq", "value": "free" }, { "kind": "not", "child": { "kind": "event", "event": "used_csv_export" } } ] } }`

path.description: JSON Pointer into the expression document.

suggestions.description: Bounded similar observed names for likely typos.

audienceVersionId.description: The pinned immutable audience version (aud_…). Null only for campaigns still stored with the deprecated legacy targeting shape.

reason.description: Why this audience version was created.

legacy.description: True when derived from a stored legacy targeting shape rather than a pinned audience version.

oneOf.description: The stored audience cannot be read (fails validation). The campaign delivers to NOBODY until the audience is replaced — invalid audiences fail closed, never widen to everyone.

segmentVersion.description: The exact pinned version — later segment revisions never change it.

oneOf.description: A saved segment version pinned by this campaign.

CampaignAudience.description: The campaign's effective audience: everyone (`all`), a pinned inline expression, a pinned saved segment version (`segment`), or `invalid` (fail-closed).

key.description: Stable project-unique machine key (lowercase slug). Reference segments by id or key everywhere.

description.description: The audience's intent — not a duplicate rendering of its rules.

currentVersion.description: The segment's current version number; campaign writes that omit a version pin this.

currentAudienceVersionId.description: The immutable audience version (aud_…) behind the current version.

summary.description: Deterministically derived readable summary of the current expression.

expression.description: The current version's exact canonical expression.

reason.description: Why the current version was created or revised.

serving.description: `ok` means web in-app messages are being served. `payment_required` means billing must be restored before either channel can deliver. `cap_reached` means usage reached the organization's spend cap for this period.

emailServing.description: Campaign-email serving state. It is `paused` whenever `serving` is not `ok`, and while billing is past_due even though web in-app keeps serving.

billable.description: Whether a payment method is on file.

boundary.description: Organizations with a payment method follow their subscription period; the rest follow the UTC calendar month.

activeUsers.description: Monthly active users across the organization in this period. An end user counts once per period in each project when identified, tracked, shown a web in-app message, or accepted for campaign email.

frequencyCapped.description: Campaign-email deliveries skipped by the recipient frequency limit during the current period, across the organization.

estimatedSpendUsd.description: Usage cost so far in USD, before tax.

spendCapUsd.description: The organization's spend cap in USD, or null when no cap is set.

projects.description: Monthly active users and frequency-capped campaign-email deliveries per project in this period.

frequencyCapped.description: Campaign-email deliveries skipped by the recipient frequency limit during the current period.

evaluatedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds. The single instant used for every count in this response.

endUsers.description: All identified end-users in the project.

eventsLast7d.description: Events tracked at or after `evaluatedAt` minus seven days.

activeCampaigns.description: Campaigns whose stored status is `running`, including rows whose delivery window is scheduled or expired.

impressions.description: Deliveries with a `shownAt` timestamp in the bucket.

clicks.description: Deliveries with a `clickedAt` timestamp in the bucket.

conversions.description: Deliveries with a `convertedAt` timestamp in the bucket.

startAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at the start of the UTC day.

evaluatedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds. The single instant used for every bucket in this response.

days.description: One dense entry per UTC day, ending with the day that contains `evaluatedAt`.

topEvents.description: Most frequent event names in the range, by count descending then name ascending.

hasAnyActivity.description: True when the project has any delivery ever, or any event or impression inside the range.

evaluatedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds. The single instant used for every count in this response.

totalUsers.description: All identified end-users in the project, with no time filter.

activeUsers.description: Users whose `lastSeenAt` is at or after `startAt`.

newUsers.description: Users whose `firstSeenAt` is at or after `startAt`.

AgentRunReferences.description: Names for the first-class `goalId` and `campaignId` values on the returned runs. Free-form run JSON is never inspected.

BadRequest.description: Invalid JSON, missing or invalid fields, or wrong content type.

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid API key. SDK endpoints take the publishable key; management endpoints (campaigns, media, users, events, goals, agent runs) take the secret key.

TooLarge.description: Request body exceeds the endpoint's size limit.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded, counted per project (SDK endpoints: 120 requests/minute or 2,000/hour per endpoint; management endpoints: 60/minute or 1,000/hour per resource group — all campaign operations share one budget, as do goal operations and user reads). Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

ServerError.description: Galinum could not complete the request.

x-mcp.instructions:
Galinum is self-driving product communications. You use it to create, target,
launch, and measure product messages for one project. The project secret you
authenticated with scopes every call to that project.

## Classify the request before you write

Decide which of three modes the user asked for, then use the smallest one:

- **Direct** — one message, engagement stats only. "Announce the CSV export",
  "tell free users about the promo", "draft a message about the pricing change".
- **Outcome-measured** — one message plus a goal you measure. "Send the promo
  and track upgrades", "tell me whether people start using it".
- **Optimized** — variants and goal-driven optimization. "A/B test this
  message", "optimize onboarding", "work toward the activation goal".

Direct is the default. Never add a goal, variants, a delivery window, an
evaluation, or optimization that the user did not ask for. A product having
goals does not make an ordinary announcement outcome-measured. Use one message
for direct communication. Set a delivery window only from timing the user gave
you, or after you resolve the missing dates with them.

## Respect launch authority

If the user said draft, propose, or prepare, stop at draft. Never launch.

Launch only when the user gave explicit launch, send, or announce authority.
If launch authority is ambiguous, stop at draft and ask the user.

## Check what already exists before you write

Before you create, launch, or update a campaign:

1. Read recent agent runs, so you can see what another agent already did.
2. Query running campaigns and scheduled campaigns as two separate calls.
3. Read every page through `pageCount` for both status queries.
4. Treat the deduplicated union as a complete point-in-time snapshot only
   after both paginated searches are exhausted.
5. Repeat both queries immediately before the write.

This snapshot never protects you against a concurrent campaign write. Do not
claim that it does. Avoid overlapping audiences and delivery periods.

## Log decisions, and never double-write

Log material decisions, proposals, and launches as agent runs. Reuse the same
idempotency key when you retry, so one decision produces one run record.

Never retry an uncertain campaign creation. Read campaigns back and confirm
what exists first. For any other uncertain write, read the current state before
you act again.
x-mcp.readonlyInstructions: This endpoint exposes read-only tools only. Campaign, goal, and segment writes are not available here. Connect to the full endpoint when the user asks you to create, update, or launch something.
